entries.originalText: Oh most blessed mansion of the City which is above!
entries.modernizedText: Oh, most blessed dwelling of the City above!

entries.originalText: Oh most clear day of eternity which the night obscureth not, but the Supreme Truth ever enlighteneth!
entries.modernizedText: Oh, most bright day of eternity, which night does not darken, but which the Supreme Truth forever enlightens!

entries.originalText: Day always joyful, always secure and never changing its state into those which are contrary.
entries.modernizedText: A day always joyful, always secure, and never changing into its opposite.

entries.originalText: Oh would that this day might shine forth, and that all these temporal things would come to an end.
entries.modernizedText: Oh, that this day might shine forth and all these temporal things come to an end.

entries.originalText: It shineth indeed upon the Saints, glowing with unending brightness, but only from afar and through a glass, upon those who are pilgrims on the earth.
entries.modernizedText: It shines indeed upon the Saints, glowing with unending brightness, but only from afar and through a glass upon those who are pilgrims on earth.

entries.originalText: The citizens of heaven know how glorious that day is; the exiled sons of Eve groan, because this is bitter and wearisome.
entries.modernizedText: The citizens of heaven know how glorious that day is; the exiled children of Eve groan because this life is bitter and wearisome.

entries.originalText: The days of this life are few and evil, full of sorrows and straits, where man is defiled with many sins, ensnared with many passions, bound fast with many fears, wearied with many cares, distracted with many questionings, entangled with many vanities, compassed about with many errors, worn away with many labours, weighed down with temptations, enervated by pleasures, tormented by poverty.
entries.modernizedText: The days of this life are few and evil, full of sorrows and hardships, in which a person is defiled with many sins, ensnared by many passions, bound fast by many fears, wearied by many cares, distracted by many questions, entangled in many vanities, surrounded by many errors, worn down by many labors, weighed down by temptations, weakened by pleasures, and tormented by poverty.

entries.originalText: Oh when shall there be an end of these evils?
entries.modernizedText: Oh, when will these evils end?

entries.originalText: When shall I be delivered from the wretched slavery of my sins?
entries.modernizedText: When will I be delivered from the wretched slavery of my sins?

entries.originalText: When shall I be mindful, O Lord, of Thee alone?
entries.modernizedText: When, O Lord, will I be mindful of You alone?

entries.originalText: When shall I rejoice in Thee to the full?
entries.modernizedText: When will I rejoice in You fully?

entries.originalText: When shall I be in true liberty without any impediment, without any burden on mind or body?
entries.modernizedText: When will I be in true freedom, without any hindrance, without any burden on mind or body?

entries.originalText: When shall there be solid peace, peace immovable and secure, peace within and without, peace firm on every side?
entries.modernizedText: When will there be solid peace, peace unshakable and secure, peace within and without, peace firm on every side?

entries.originalText: Blessed Jesus, when shall I stand to behold Thee?
entries.modernizedText: Blessed Jesus, when will I stand and behold You?

entries.originalText: When shall I gaze upon the glory of Thy kingdom?
entries.modernizedText: When will I gaze upon the glory of Your kingdom?

entries.originalText: When shalt Thou be to me all in all?
entries.modernizedText: When will You be to me all in all?

entries.originalText: Oh when shall I be with Thee in Thy Kingdom which Thou hast prepared from the foundation of the world for them that love Thee?
entries.modernizedText: Oh, when will I be with You in Your Kingdom, which You have prepared from the foundation of the world for those who love You?

entries.originalText: I am left destitute, an exile in a hostile land, where are daily wars and grievous misfortunes.
entries.modernizedText: I am left destitute, an exile in a hostile land, where there are daily wars and grievous misfortunes.

entries.originalText: Console my exile, mitigate my sorrow, for towards Thee all my desire longeth.
entries.modernizedText: Comfort me in my exile, ease my sorrow, for all my desire longs toward You.

entries.originalText: For all is to me a burden, whatsoever this world offereth for consolation.
entries.modernizedText: For whatever this world offers for consolation is a burden to me.

entries.originalText: I yearn to enjoy Thee intimately, but I cannot attain unto it.
entries.modernizedText: I yearn to enjoy You intimately, but I cannot attain it.

entries.originalText: I long to cleave to heavenly things, but temporal things and unmortified passions press me down.
entries.modernizedText: I long to cling to heavenly things, but temporal things and unmortified passions press me down.

entries.originalText: In my mind I would be above all things, but in my flesh I am unwillingly compelled to be beneath them.
entries.modernizedText: In my mind I would be above all things, but in my flesh I am unwillingly compelled to be beneath them.

entries.originalText: So, wretched man that I am, I fight with myself, and am made grievous even unto myself, while the spirit seeketh to be above and the flesh to be beneath.
entries.modernizedText: So, wretched man that I am, I fight with myself and am burdensome even to myself, while the spirit seeks to be above and the flesh beneath.

entries.originalText: Oh how I suffer inwardly, while with the mind I discourse on heavenly things, and presently a crowd of carnal things rusheth upon me whilst I pray.
entries.modernizedText: Oh, how I suffer inwardly when I speak in my mind of heavenly things, and soon a crowd of carnal things rushes upon me while I pray.

entries.originalText: My God, be not Thou far from me, nor depart in wrath from Thy servant.
entries.modernizedText: My God, do not be far from me, nor depart in anger from Your servant.

entries.originalText: Cast forth Thy lightning and scatter them; send out Thine arrows,(1) and let all delusions of my enemy be confounded.
entries.modernizedText: Cast forth Your lightning and scatter them; send out Your arrows,(1) and let all the delusions of my enemy be confounded.

entries.originalText: Recall my senses unto Thyself, cause me to forget all worldly things; grant me quickly to cast away and despise the imaginations of sin.
entries.modernizedText: Recall my senses to Yourself, cause me to forget all worldly things, and grant me quickly to cast away and despise sinful imaginations.

entries.originalText: Succour me, O Eternal Truth, that no vanity may move me.
entries.modernizedText: Help me, O Eternal Truth, so that no vanity may move me.

entries.originalText: Come unto me, O Heavenly Sweetness, and let all impurity flee from before Thy face.
entries.modernizedText: Come to me, O Heavenly Sweetness, and let all impurity flee from Your presence.

entries.originalText: Pardon me also, and of Thy mercy deal gently with me, whensoever in prayer I think on anything besides Thee; for truly I confess that I am wont to be continually distracted.
entries.modernizedText: Pardon me also, and in Your mercy deal gently with me whenever in prayer I think of anything besides You; for I truly confess that I am continually distracted.

entries.originalText: For often and often, where in the body I stand or sit, there I myself am not; but rather am I there, whither I am borne by my thoughts.
entries.modernizedText: For often and often I myself am not where I stand or sit in body; rather I am where my thoughts carry me.

entries.originalText: Where my thought is, there am I; and there commonly is my thought where that which I love is.
entries.modernizedText: Where my thought is, there am I; and my thought is usually where what I love is.

entries.originalText: That readily occurreth to me, which naturally delighteth, or pleaseth through custom.
entries.modernizedText: What naturally delights me or pleases me through habit readily comes to mind.

entries.originalText: Wherefore Thou, who art the Truth, hast plainly said, Where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.(2) If I love heaven, I gladly meditate on heavenly things.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore You, who are the Truth, have plainly said, Where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.(2) If I love heaven, I gladly meditate on heavenly things.

entries.originalText: If I love the world, I rejoice in the delights of the world, and am made sorry by its adversities.
entries.modernizedText: If I love the world, I rejoice in the delights of the world and am saddened by its adversities.

entries.originalText: If I love the flesh, I am continually imagining the things which belong to the flesh; if I love the spirit, I am delighted by meditating on spiritual things.
entries.modernizedText: If I love the flesh, I continually imagine the things that belong to the flesh; if I love the spirit, I delight in meditating on spiritual things.

entries.originalText: For whatsoever things I love, on these I readily converse and listen, and carry home with me the images of them.
entries.modernizedText: For whatever things I love, I readily speak and listen about them and carry their images home with me.

entries.originalText: But blessed is that man who for Thy sake, O Lord, is willing to part from all creatures; who doth violence to his fleshly nature and crucifieth the lusts of the flesh by the fervour of his spirit, so that with serene conscience he may offer unto Thee a pure prayer, and be made worthy to enter into the angelic choirs, having shut out from himself, both outwardly and inwardly, all worldly things.
entries.modernizedText: But blessed is the person who for Your sake, O Lord, is willing to part from all creatures; who does violence to his fleshly nature and crucifies the lusts of the flesh by the fervor of his spirit, so that with a serene conscience he may offer You a pure prayer and be made worthy to enter the angelic choirs, having shut out from himself, both outwardly and inwardly, all worldly things.
